body.html: Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel — Kim Jek Sin 2 in Thai — is a 2-star budget hotel of around 30 rooms on Phithak Phanomket Road in the heart of Mukdahan town, near the provincial hall and government quarter. The selling point isn't luxury; it's a very light price and spacious free parking. It's a simple in-town hotel with a 24-hour front desk and a small on-site restaurant — a good fit for travelers who use the room just to sleep, then head out to run errands or explore the city.

Rooms come as Standard Twin (two single beds) and Standard Double (one large bed). They're simply furnished and practical, with air conditioning, a TV, a fridge, a desk and an en-suite bathroom with shower. A recurring compliment is that rooms are clean and feel larger than expected for the price. The common gripes are that walls are fairly thin, so you can hear neighboring rooms, and some rooms carry a slight musty smell typical of an older building — if a room isn't right, you can ask to switch at check-in.
"Very cheap, big parking lot, room clean enough. Central location — you can walk to the market and the Mekong. Friendly staff. Perfect for a no-fuss stopover in Mukdahan without paying much."

Location is the advantage here. The hotel sits in the city center on Phithak Phanomket Road, near the provincial hall and government quarter, within easy walking distance of the Indochina Market and the Mekong riverside promenade. Restaurants, cafes and convenience stores are all within walking reach. Ho Kaeo Mukdahan Tower and the 2nd Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge (Mukdahan-Savannakhet) are about 10-15 minutes by car, making it a handy base before crossing into Laos or touring the lower Isan region.

On facilities, set expectations to match a budget property. There's free Wi-Fi and free private parking — and the lot is spacious, which self-drivers love. There's a small on-site restaurant, but no pool, and breakfast usually isn't included; there are plenty of eateries and coffee shops within a short walk. The repeated gripes in reviews are thin walls with sound carrying between rooms, and Wi-Fi that drops out at times, so it pays to keep expectations in line with the price.

Straight talk: Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel suits travelers after the cheapest walkable in-town base with easy parking, who aren't fussy about a new building or perfect quiet. If you're here for errands, government business, a stopover before crossing into Laos, or city sightseeing where you only use the room to sleep, it fits well on value. The overall guest score sits around 8.0, which is solid for a hotel at this price, and most guests are happy once expectations are set at a 2-star level. The knocks you'll see are thin walls, a musty smell in some rooms and an aging building.

A tip from following the reviews: ask for a room on a higher floor or a corner that isn't directly next to others to help with sound carrying through the walls. If smell matters to you, ask for a freshly cleaned room and let the air conditioning run for a while before settling in. If you're driving, parking is free and spacious. And since it's in town, stroll to the Mekong promenade and Indochina Market in the evening for the breeze and views across to Laos, then grab a bite nearby.

honestSummary: Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel sells the lightest price in town, free spacious parking and a central location — near the provincial hall, within walking distance of the Indochina Market and the Mekong riverside, with clean-enough rooms and friendly staff. It works for budget travelers, errand-runners and anyone stopping over before crossing into Laos. The trade-off is an older building with fairly thin walls, a musty smell in some rooms, and fewer facilities than a larger hotel.
honestChecks: If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — walls are fairly thin and some reviews report sound carrying from neighboring rooms and the corridor → ask for a higher floor or corner room and pack earplugs just in case.

If you want full facilities like a pool or breakfast — this is a 2-star budget hotel with no pool and breakfast usually not included → for the full package, choose a higher-tier hotel in town instead.
If you want a Mekong river view straight from your room — it's in town and walkable to the river but not on the waterfront → for river views, pick a riverside hotel instead.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel Mukdahan

faq.q: Where is Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel and how do I get there?
faq.a: It's at 95/1 Phithak Phanomket Road in the heart of Mukdahan town, near the provincial hall and government quarter. It's within easy walking distance of the Indochina Market and the Mekong riverside promenade, with restaurants and convenience stores within reach. Ho Kaeo Mukdahan Tower and the 2nd Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge are about 10-15 minutes by car — handy as a stopover before crossing to Savannakhet. There's free, spacious parking on site.

faq.q: What are room prices at Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel and what types are there?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿350/night for a Standard Twin. A Standard Double runs around ฿400, and a standard room for two around ฿450. Every room has air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and an en-suite bathroom. Prices vary by season and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel have breakfast and a pool?
faq.a: This is a 2-star budget hotel — there's no pool and breakfast usually isn't included. There's a small on-site restaurant, and plenty of eateries, coffee shops and convenience stores within a short walk. The hotel does have free Wi-Fi, free private parking and a 24-hour front desk.

faq.q: What are the rooms like — are they clean?
faq.a: Rooms are simply furnished and practical, and mostly clean and larger than expected for this price point, with air conditioning, a TV, a fridge and an en-suite bathroom with shower. Some reviews note thin walls with sound carrying from neighboring rooms, or a slight musty smell in some rooms — you can ask to switch rooms at check-in if it bothers you.

faq.q: Who is Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for budget travelers who want the cheapest walkable in-town base with easy parking — errand-runners, those on government business, city sightseers who only use the room to sleep, and anyone stopping over before crossing into Laos. It's especially convenient for self-drivers thanks to the free, spacious parking, and less suited to those expecting a new building or full facilities.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Kim Jek Cin 2 Hotel?
faq.a: The hotel is an older building with fairly thin walls. The repeated gripes are sound carrying from neighboring rooms, a musty smell in some rooms, and Wi-Fi that drops out at times — keep expectations in line with a 2-star price. It's not directly on the Mekong, though the riverside is walkable. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a higher floor and pack earplugs. During festivals or town events, rooms fill fast, so book ahead.
